title: LiPM: Foundation Model for Lithium-Ion Battery Analysis

problem.claim: Existing deep learning methods for lithium-ion battery analysis are narrow in battery-type and task coverage.

gap.claim: Existing time-series pretraining models do not adequately model battery data's physicochemical complexity and irregular timing.

contributions.claim: LiPM is a pretrained foundation model that combines learning across multiple datasets using physics-aware objectives and temporal modeling tolerant of irregular sampling.
The model combines mixed masked reconstruction, a charge-conservation regression task, and dual-scale temporal encoding.
LiPM is trained across eight heterogeneous battery datasets without cycle-label annotations and is intended to operate across partial charge-discharge segments and irregular sampling protocols.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report applicability across partial charge-discharge segments and irregular sampling protocols.
The authors report improvements over nine state-of-the-art baselines on downstream tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Battery-analysis deep learning methods are specialized and limited in scope.
Current time-series pretraining methods insufficiently capture battery-specific physical complexity and irregular temporal structure.
LiPM addresses the gap through multi-dataset pretraining with physics-aware objectives and irregularity-tolerant temporal modeling.
The model is trained on eight heterogeneous datasets without cycle labels and evaluated across varied battery segments and sampling protocols.
The authors report gains over nine state-of-the-art baselines on downstream tasks.

source_observation.claim: The model incorporates domain constraints and handles irregular temporal observations during pretraining.

interpretation.claim: For scientific time-series foundation models, representation learning may benefit from encoding known physical structure and observation irregularity.

application.claim: Use domain-consistency objectives and time-aware modeling when building models for irregular scientific sensor data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that these design choices generalize beyond lithium-ion battery data or all scientific time series.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify downstream tasks, quantitative improvement values, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, model scale, or implementation and reproducibility details.
